newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices spurt on higher export quota.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices spurt on higher export quota.

text.p: Cotton prices extended gains on Wednesday spurred by speculative activity caused by the government's permission to allow more exports, dealer said.
But mill owners purchases were limited, they said.
Bengaldeshi ready delivery moved up by 15/30 rupees to 850/900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while November delivery looked up by same margin at 920/925 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium staple) quoted steady at 12,500/12,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). So was Wagad variety at 10,900/11,000 rupees per candy, traders said.
Traders were expecting a price rise in Bengaldeshi cotton to be shortlived in view of the rising new crop arrivals.
